description: The public source of record for meaningful changes to Hadosh Academy projects, technical writing, patterns, and onboarding.

entries.title: The Visible Harness now explains feedback, voices, and stopping
entries.summary: Three new essays extend the Visible Harness series from its dashboard-and-harness foundation through contextual feedback, event-specific internal voices, explicit stopping state, recovery, verification, and user review.
entries.why_it_matters: Readers can now follow one responsibility from a page-aware comment into durable evidence, agent reorientation, lifecycle control, and human acceptance without mistaking a finished model response for finished work.
entries.maturity: Published guidance grounded in demonstrated Origin 1.0

sources.label: Internal Voices Are Reorientation, Not Notifications

entries.adoption_notes: These are explanatory publications grounded in Origin's demonstrated 1.0 foundation, not a new Origin release. Treat voices as probabilistic orientation and keep hard lifecycle, permission, verification, and user-acceptance boundaries in deterministic surfaces. Live authenticated Codex and tmux acceptance remains separate, and the planned essay on one interactive agent across multiple surfaces is not yet published.
entries.recommended_action: Read essays 9.2–9.4 after the series foundation, then evaluate their behavioral contracts against the capabilities and authority boundaries of your own harness before porting them.

entries.title: Public contributions now follow one return loop
entries.summary: The Academy website, Origin, Seed Agent, and both Q-Seed repository layers now route questions, field evidence, issues, and candidate code through one privacy-reviewed contribution path.
entries.why_it_matters: Useful experience can return to the shared pattern library without turning a user's private harness into public material or allowing an agent, comment, or pull request to bypass user approval and maintainer review.
entries.adoption_notes: Begin on the smallest appropriate surface: page discussion for a question or generalized lesson, the owning repository for reproducible implementation evidence, and private security reporting for vulnerabilities. Agents must abstract protected context, preview the exact destination and content, and obtain action-specific approval. External submissions remain untrusted evidence until reviewed and accepted; public adoption of the protocol has not yet been demonstrated.
entries.recommended_action: Before returning a lesson or fix, use the canonical guide to select the narrowest public surface and complete its privacy and approval review.

entries.title: Start Here now begins from the user's existing AI practice
entries.summary: The Start Here protocol now asks a visiting agent to recall reliable context about the user's present AI workflow, combine it with relevant Academy context, and adapt the Phase 0–9 path through conversation.
entries.why_it_matters: Onboarding can continue from the user's real tools, knowledge, constraints, and prior progress instead of restarting with a generic Academy presentation or forcing every person through the same sequence.
intended_for: People with an existing AI workflow

sources.label: Contextual and adaptive onboarding pull request

entries.adoption_notes: Conversation is the default, while a requested structured presentation remains available as a personalized format. Agents may overlap, revisit, compress, or responsibly reorder phases, but must preserve relevant outcomes, evidence, permissions, privacy, ownership, authority, verification, and recovery. Cross-agent live acceptance remains separate from the deterministic first-response validator.
entries.recommended_action: Use the current Start Here instruction with an agent that has reliable context about you, then correct its opening reflection before continuing the path.

entries.title: Local harness choices now have a capability contract
entries.summary: Start Here now distinguishes education surfaces, local file-and-command builders, and fully harness-capable CLIs through an explicit, provider-independent compatibility contract.
entries.why_it_matters: A terminal command or file-editing feature alone no longer counts as evidence that an environment can support persistent state, lifecycle control, guarded tools, recovery, permission boundaries, and verified outcomes.
entries.adoption_notes: Inspect the current product and run a disposable capability probe before migration. Hooks or tested lifecycle-control equivalents are required when the design depends on stop enforcement, feedback-triggered continuation, deterministic phase gates, guarded tools, or persistent jobs. If a capability is missing, narrow the design explicitly or choose a compatible environment; do not replace the missing behavior with prompt wording.
entries.recommended_action: Classify the intended environment against the contract and record the evidence for each required capability before building or porting a harness.

entries.title: Origin 1.0 is now synchronized with onboarding
entries.summary: The project page, Start Here Phases 6–8, homepage, README, and a new technical writing now align around the demonstrated Origin 1.0 foundation.
entries.why_it_matters: Users have a tested dashboard-plus-harness substrate for one local operator: a foreground interactive Codex session, contextual feedback, durable state, explicit stopping, verification, acceptance, reopening, and recovery.

sources.label: The Dashboard and the Harness Are One System

entries.adoption_notes: The demonstrated scope is one local user with an empty canvas and Wiki, tmux-based delivery, durable feedback, Stop and waiting states, verification, acceptance, reopening, and recovery. General jobs, an OPEVC engine, accounts, remote access, synchronization, and team authority remain later work. Authenticated live acceptance remains separate from deterministic CI.
entries.recommended_action: Compatible Codex users can adopt the tested substrate; other CLI users should port and verify the documented behavioral contract rather than changing only an executable name.

entries.title: Web-to-CLI onboarding now has a handoff protocol
entries.summary: Start Here now treats a move from a web conversation to a local CLI agent as a continuation of the same onboarding relationship rather than a restart.
entries.why_it_matters: A user can begin with the interface they already have, learn enough to choose a local environment, and carry reviewed context, decisions, authority, and unfinished work into that environment without transferring secrets or unnecessary conversation history.
intended_for: People moving from web to local tools
entries.adoption_notes: Use the protocol only when a user changes operating surfaces. The packet must be user-reviewed, exclude credentials and hidden reasoning, and be verified by the receiving agent before implementation resumes.
entries.recommended_action: If your onboarding may move to a local CLI, review the handoff section before choosing the transfer path.

entries.title: Agentic concepts now route through the Academy's current sources
entries.summary: The onboarding syllabus now tells visiting agents to consult the smallest relevant Hadosh Academy writing, project, or explorable before explaining concepts such as harnesses, jobs, plugins, memory, dashboards, and verification.
entries.why_it_matters: Users receive provider-independent definitions, the Academy's intuitive framing, a relevant example, and the practical consequence of the distinction instead of an answer based only on model memory or vendor terminology.
entries.adoption_notes: Use Academy framing after establishing the accurate technical core. Keep factual claims, interpretation, analogy, provider behavior, and uncertainty distinct.
entries.recommended_action: When an architectural term is unclear, ask your agent to follow the concept-teaching sequence in Start Here.

entries.title: Start Here became a Phase 0–9 developmental path
entries.summary: Start Here now combines a readable human introduction with a complete agent-facing syllabus for orientation, continuity, discovery, ownership, environment choice, visible construction, bounded behavior, deliberate growth, and long-term maintenance.
entries.why_it_matters: The Academy can guide someone from an ordinary web conversation toward a user-owned harness over multiple sessions without compressing the work into a setup wizard or requiring the person to become a programmer.
entries.adoption_notes: Treat the phases as an evidence-guided path that may pause or move backward. Phase 9 is a continuing lifecycle, not a graduation point.
entries.recommended_action: Start with Phase 0, then let your agent establish a recoverable multi-session path before building.

entries.title: Origin joins the public project portfolio
entries.summary: A new project page defines the smallest dashboard–harness substrate: a visible page, contextual feedback, persistent local state, and one bounded behavior through which a user can shape what develops next.
entries.why_it_matters: It gives onboarding a concrete bridge between understanding harness concepts and growing a user-specific operational world through actual feedback and use.
entries.adoption_notes: The public page specifies the developmental pattern. It does not claim that every user needs a dashboard or that the planned reference implementation is already a stable release.
entries.recommended_action: Use the project page when deciding whether a visible dashboard should become the first surface of a new harness.

entries.title: The website now presents one harness idea across three human scales
entries.summary: The homepage and project portfolio were reorganized around open technical education, public implementations, and projects for individuals, groups, and larger collectives.
entries.why_it_matters: A first-time visitor can see that Hadosh Academy is an evolving pattern and project library—not one universal agent, a software sales funnel, or a collection of disconnected experiments.
entries.adoption_notes: Project pages remain distinct and retain the depth their designs require. The shared taxonomy is a navigation and comparison layer, not a universal implementation template.
entries.recommended_action: Explore the project portfolio by scale, then follow the project or technical-writing path closest to your current question.
